layers.note: Shares the canopy of moist lowland forest with Douglas-fir and redcedar and fills the understory beneath them; the climax tree of western Washington lowlands.

moisture.note: Moist ground: lower slopes, benches and ravines; scarce on dry, sunny sites and in standing water.

heat_load.note: Favours cool, shaded aspects and ravines; scarce on hot south-west slopes.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,000 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

shade_tolerance.note: Among the most shade-tolerant trees in the region: it regenerates under a closed canopy.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −6 °C, gone by −12 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −28 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −36 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 12.5 to 23 °C; gone below 10 °C, where summers are too short, and above 26.5 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long cool growing season: about 2,300 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,000 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 550: the warmth of the maritime lowlands and lower mountain slopes.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.62, gone by 0.5.

summer_rain.note: The summer-dry Pacific climate: no lower limit; its range lies where at most about 0.4 of the year's precipitation falls in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Western hemlock grows from south-central Alaska to north-west California near the coast, and inland in the wet belt to Idaho and Montana (Silvics of North America, vol. 1). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
